title: Cross-functional rollout canvas + inspection checklist (working)
content:
Purpose: quick, shareable canvas for planning cross-functional rollouts and a running inspection checklist for canary / A/B style launches. This is intentionally concise so teams can copy the canvas into feature-specific docs and iterate.

Status: working draft — meant to be used during kickoff and pre-traffic checkpoints. Keep iterations small; capture learnings here rather than waiting for a pretty Confluence page.

1) One-line launch thesis
- What problem are we solving? (customer-visible symptom + impact metric)
- Hypothesis: bundle of change + expected metric delta (primary + guardrail metrics)

Example: "Reduce median latency for chat streaming by 25% for hosted-api free tier by switching to batching-enabled runtime path, without increasing error rate >0.05 percentage points."

2) Cross-functional owners (RACI-lite)
- Product: Maya Chen — outcome owner, decision gate lead
- Eng (Serving runtime): Arjun Patel — rollout plan, canary infra, rollback automation
- Eng (Console): Liam O'Connor — feature flags, routing config, observability hooks
- SRE: Sofia Martinez — SLO guardrails, escalations, runbook updates
- Security/Compliance: assigned as needed for private deployments
- Customer Success: optional for targeted customers in canary cohort

3) Experiment / rollout design summary (copy into tickets)
- Variant A (control): current serving path
- Variant B (treatment): new batching runtime w/ KV prefix caching enabled
- Traffic partitioning: staged allocation 0.1% -> 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100% with hold windows
- Duration per stage: 30m for early micro, 2 hours for broader, 24–72h for final validations
- Allocation method: cookie+user-id hashing for persistent assignment; use feature-flag gating for quick reversion

4) Primary metrics + guardrails (define exact queries + dashboards)
- Primary metric: median end-to-end response latency (ms) for streaming completions — SQL metric id: LAT-MED-V1
- Secondary: 95th percentile latency, throughput (requests/sec), cost per token
- Guardrails: error rate (500/502/504) < 0.05pp increase; token loss incidents = 0; customer impact tickets = 0 during canary windows
- Observability required: per-route latency histogram, model-variant tag, infra-level GPU utilization, queueing latency, prefix-cache hit rate

5) Success criteria & decision gates (pass/fail rules, who signs off)
- Micro-canary (0.1%): no severe errors for 30m and latency median <= baseline*0.9 -> proceed
- Broader canary (1–5%): no guardrail violations for 2h, SRE reads logs and confirms no resource pressure -> proceed
- Ramp to 20%: business/PD approval; CS notified for customer outreach
- Full rollout: product sign-off after 24–72h stable metrics
- Rollback trigger list: >0.05pp error increase, sustained 95th percentile latency regression >15%, or unexpected cost blowout >30%

6) Observability & data plumbing checklist (must be in place before any traffic)
- Dashboards: feature-flag variant split, per-variant latency distributions, error breakdown by code, infra metrics (GPU mem, CPU steal), prefix cache hit ratio
- Traces: spans must include experiment id, variant tag, and route id. Ensure sampling policy surfaces tail traces.
- Logging: structured logs include request_id, variant, model_version, user_hash. Redact PII.
- Telemetry schema: event names and fields mapped to analytics (metric ids listed above). Owner: Eng-Observability

7) Canary automation and safety nets
- Auto-suppress ramp if error rate > threshold for X minutes (configurable)
- Auto-fallback route: route to nearest compatible model variant in different capacity pool if GPU pressure spikes
- Feature-flag quick kill: console path + API to set 100% to control within 30s (test before launch)
- SRE Pager: integrate pager for specific alarm threshold channels

8) Communication plan (who to ping and when)
- Kickoff: announce in #rollouts + email to CS & sales with expected windows and impact
- Micro-canary start: @SRE on-call, product lead, eng lead in thread
- Each ramp step: short summary in thread with dashboard snapshot and commit link
- Incident/rollback: immediate page to SRE + notify exec owner

9) Customer-specific considerations
- For Dedicated/Private customers: check config drift and network egress patterns before routing any traffic; require CS opt-in for early cohorts
- Data residency: ensure telemetry export targets do not break residency constraints; Security to sign off

10) Evaluation template (fill after each ramp step)
- Step: <percentage> | Duration | Key observations | Primary metric delta | Guardrail violations | Action (proceed/hold/rollback) | Signed-off-by

11) Post-rollout retrospective prompts
- Were we able to attribute outcome to the change? (confounding factors, coincident infra events)
- Telemetry gaps discovered? (missing fields, dashboards slow to update)
- Which manual checks can be automated next time?
- Customer feedback captured? any support tickets?

12) Short TODOs / open questions (notes to self)
- TODO: add exact SQL snippets for LAT-MED-V1 and 95p queries (Arjun)
- TODO: test feature-flag kill path from console (Liam)
- Open: how to handle persistent cohort assignment for anonymous users across device clears? (proposal: store minimal assignment cookie + fallback by consistent hashing)
- Open: threshold tuning for low-traffic features — shorter hold windows or synthetic traffic? (propose synthetic litmus tests for infra pressure)

13) Quick commands (ops cheatsheet) — test or QA only, do not run in prod without SRE oversight
- Kill flag: curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/flags/kill?feature=<id>
- Check variant split: select count(*) by variant from analytics.events where experiment_id="EX-xxxx" and ts > now() - interval '1h'
- Rollback: run rollout-runbook -> set route weights to 0% treatment, 100% control; validate

Appendix: related artifacts and starting point links
- Existing rollouts to reference: ENG-3311 (routing-slices), PRD: rollout-traffic-partitioning-v2, Staged launch playbook (internal)

Notes on tone and usage: copy this canvas template into feature-specific drive doc at kickoff. Keep this file as the canonical lightweight checklist; heavier documentation (runbooks, postmortems) should live in Confluence linked from here.

Last edited by Maya Chen — fragmented thoughts included intentionally. If you copy sections into an official playbook, please grab the evaluation template and the auto-suppress configs verbatim.
